topic: What if you never needed to sleep?
title: WHAT IF YOU NEVER
NEEDED TO SLEEP?

power.rule: you never sleep: the whole night is yours, and you never tire
power.look: Pip's eyes glint cyan, the night's clock jumps hour to hour, an AWAKE chip beside his head

script.text: No sleep. Midnight. Three more levels.
No sleep. Two a.m. Homework, done.
No sleep. Four a.m. Everyone's asleep. Everyone but you.
What if you never needed to sleep?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: sleep is when your brain flushes its waste. A day awake, and your reaction time matches a drunk driver's. That's real.
So how long could you last?

science.claim: Sleep is when your brain flushes its waste.
science.working: The glymphatic system: during sleep, cerebrospinal fluid influx into the brain rises sharply, the interstitial space widens, and waste (including beta-amyloid) is cleared far faster than while awake — clearance of soluble amyloid-beta measured about twice as fast in sleeping mice. Wakefulness means the flush mostly stops, so 'never sleep' means the waste never goes.
science.source: Xie et al., 'Sleep Drives Metabolite Clearance from the Adult Brain', Science 342, 373 (18 Oct 2013, Nedergaard lab, Univ. of Rochester)

science.claim: A day awake (24 hours without sleep), and your reaction time matches a drunk driver's.
science.working: Dawson & Reid, Nature 395, 115 (1997) 'Fatigue, alcohol and performance impairment': psychomotor performance lost after 17 h awake was equivalent to about 0.05% blood alcohol, and the equivalent rose at roughly 0.005% BAC per hour awake — about 0.10% at 24 h, above every legal driving limit. Williamson & Feyer (Occup Environ Med 57, 649, 2000) confirmed ~17-19 h deprivation matches BAC 0.05% on reaction tasks. The script says 'a day awake' = 24 h; the schematic states the 0.05% at 17 h and 0.10% at 24 h.
science.source: Dawson & Reid, Nature 395, 115 (1997); Williamson & Feyer, Occup Environ Med 57, 649 (2000)

shots.note: Midnight: Pip sits cross-legged on the foot of the bed with the handheld, its screen lighting his face; the cat asleep at the head of the bed; moonlight in the window
the bedside alarm clock reads 00:00, red digits; Pip's mitten picking up the handheld out of frame below
Pip's face lit from below by the handheld; the eyes glint cyan; a level-complete ding, x3 floating off
the finished homework, ticks and an A+, next to the pencil and a pen cap; Pip's mitten drops the finished sheet
Two a.m.: Pip at the desk, paper stack done, shoves back, smug; the desk lamp is the only light
Four a.m.: Pip stands at the window, the city black outside, the moon high; he has not stopped
the city through the glass: street after street of dark windows, one last light going out
Pip in the window's reflection: eyes glinting cyan, the faint city points behind; a little uncanny
the premise over the city at first light; Pip on the parapet, still awake, the handheld dark in his hand
Pip stops mid-step and looks up from the handheld: the sky is starting to turn
the brain in line drawing: blue cerebrospinal fluid sweeping in while it sleeps, waste dots washing out; SLEEP = THE FLUSH
a clock counts to 17 h and 24 h awake; a reaction bar falls to 0.05% then 0.10% BAC, past the legal limit
That's real.: Pip, the light turning warm
the sun clears the rooftops, the sky burns; Pip stands small against it, a whole night behind him
